title: Dependency heatmap and action runbook for cross-team roadmap coordination
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Produce an operational artifact (interactive heatmap + runbook) that surfaces all roadmap dependencies across Eng/Design/Security/Infra and prescribes clear owners, escalation paths, and contingency actions for each risk tier.

Scope: 1) single-pane heatmap view keyed by feature x dependency (service, infra, design asset, security review) with status, owner, ETA, and confidence score; 2) an action runbook with playbooks for High/Medium/Low dependency risk and templates for canary/fallback plans; 3) weekly sync cadence and an automated Slack + Console alerting integration for newly critical dependencies.

Success metrics: 1) Reduction in surprise cross-team blockers by 60% during the next cycle (tracked via retrospective tags); 2) 90% of high-severity dependencies have an assigned owner and documented mitigation within 5 business days; 3) decrease time-to-resolution for dependency incidents by 40%.

Key stakeholders: PMs (product-management), ENG owners (serving runtime, infra, security), Design leads, Program Management.

Deliverables: interactive heatmap (Console dashboard), runbook doc (Confluence), alerting playbook (Slack + Console), kickoff + 4-week rollout plan.

Out-of-scope: Replacing existing ticketing systems (we will link to Linear/GitHub rather than migrate tickets), broad org re-org decisions — we aim to improve coordination, not change team boundaries.

Trade-offs & decisions to date: We evaluated two approaches for visibility: (A) push metadata into existing Linear issues (higher fidelity, higher engineering cost) vs (B) a lightweight manual curation + automation pipeline that pulls key fields and supplements with a confidence score. We chose (B) for faster time-to-value with an explicit plan to iterate toward (A) if adoption metrics justify the engineering investment.

Open questions: 1) final schema for confidence scoring (proposed: owner confidence [0-100], external dependency flag, required SLA); 2) permissioning model for who can mark a dependency as mitigated; 3) whether runbook actions should generate canned PR/checklist templates.

Artifacts & links: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RVI/Dependency+Heatmap ; Prototype dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/rvi-dep-heatmap ; Initial design mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/rvi-heatmap-mockups ; Prototype script for nightly sync: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rvi-dep-sync (PR forthcoming).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heatmap shows dependencies for at least 3 active roadmap initiatives across Eng/Design/Security/Infra; 2) Each high-severity dependency has owner, ETA, confidence score, and mitigation steps documented; 3) Runbook contains escalation path, sample communication templates, and a rollback checklist; 4) Alerting integration posts to #rvi-dependencies when a dependency moves to High or misses ETA; 5) On-call rotation for dependency triage defined and scheduled for the next 8 weeks.
